He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Purdue Fort Wayne Mastodons men's basketball|Purdue Fort Wayne Mastodons]]. == High school career == Konchar played basketball for [[Community High School (West Chicago)|West Chicago High School]] in [[West Chicago, Illinois]]. In his junior season, he averaged 19.7 points, 8.8 rebounds, 3.4 assists, and two steals, leading his team in most statistical categories. They finished with a 5–22 record.{{cite web|last1=Narang|first1=Bob|title=West Chicago program making positive strides|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/ct-xpm-2013-07-01-ct-tl-sports-0704-dw-20130701-story.html|website=[[Chicago Tribune]]|access-date=June 5, 2019|date=July 1, 2013}} On February 27, 2014, as a senior, Konchar posted 45 points, 15 rebounds, eight assists, five steals, and five blocks in an 89–82 win over [[St. Charles North High School]]. With the performance, he became his school's all-time leading scorer, surpassing his head coach and 1983 graduate Bill Recchia.{{cite web|last1=Oberhelman|first1=Dave|title=Konchar's 45 lifts West Chicago over St. Charles North|url=https://basketball.dailyherald.com/article/20140227/sports/140228337/|website=[[Daily Herald (Arlington Heights, Illinois)|Daily Herald]]|access-date=June 5, 2019|date=February 27, 2014}} Konchar averaged 28.9 points, 14.1 rebounds, 4.1 assists, 3.2 steals, and 2.5 blocks per game in his senior season, earning All-Area MVP honors.{{cite web|last1=Schmid|first1=Scott|title=All-area MVP John Konchar posts jaw-dropping numbers|url=https://www.mysuburbanlife.com/2014/03/12/all-area-mvp-john-konchar-posts-jaw-dropping-numbers/a7fbzxi/|publisher=[[Suburban Life Media]]|access-date=June 5, 2019|date=March 21, 2014|archive-date=June 5, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190605163931/https://www.mysuburbanlife.com/2014/03/12/all-area-mvp-john-konchar-posts-jaw-dropping-numbers/a7fbzxi/|url-status=dead}} Despite his high school success, he was lightly recruited, with his only [[NCAA Division I]] scholarship offer coming from [[Chicago State Cougars men's basketball|Chicago State]]. A [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]] assistant coach convinced [[Indiana University – Purdue University Fort Wayne]] ([[Purdue Fort Wayne Mastodons men's basketball|IPFW]]), then a joint campus of the [[Indiana University]] (IU) and [[Purdue University system|Purdue University]] systems, to offer him a basketball scholarship.{{cite web|last1=Noie|first1=Tom|title=Notre Dame knows well of John Konchar's hoops He is the highest scorer in west chicago historyskills|url=https://www.ndinsider.com/basketball/mens/notre-dame-knows-well-of-john-konchar-s-hoops-skills/article_167c52f4-bb37-11e6-9740-736e89163212.html|publisher=Notre Dame Insider|access-date=June 5, 2019|date=December 5, 2016}} On April 25, 2015, he committed to IPFW.{{cite web|title=John Konchar - Basketball Recruiting|url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/197621/john-konchar|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=June 5, 2019}} == College career == During Konchar's college career, his basketball team represented two different universities and used three different athletic identities. In his [[2015–16 IPFW Mastodons men's basketball team|freshman season]], the school's athletic program was known as the IPFW Mastodons. Between his freshman and [[2016–17 Fort Wayne Mastodons men's basketball team|sophomore seasons]], IPFW changed its athletic branding to Fort Wayne Mastodons.{{cite press release |url=http://gomastodons.com/news/2016/8/5/GEN_080816.aspx?path=general |title=Introducing the Fort Wayne Mastodons |publisher=Fort Wayne Athletics |date=August 8, 2016 |access-date=December 16, 2016}} After his sophomore season, the IU and Purdue systems agreed to dissolve IPFW effective June 30, 2018. IPFW's degree programs in health sciences would transfer to the new [[Indiana University Fort Wayne]], while all other IPFW degree programs, plus the IPFW athletic department, would become part of the new [[Purdue University Fort Wayne]] (PFW).{{cite news|url=https://www.wowo.com/indiana-purdue-trustees-officially-finalize-ipfw-split/ |title=Indiana, Purdue trustees officially finalize IPFW split |first=Darrin |last=Wright |publisher=WOWO |location=Fort Wayne, IN |date=June 16, 2017 |access-date=January 22, 2018}} Shortly before the split became official, the athletic department announced that it would henceforth be known as the Purdue Fort Wayne Mastodons.{{cite press release |url=http://www.gomastodons.com/news/2018/6/18/general-purdue-fort-wayne-branding-released.aspx |title=Purdue Fort Wayne Branding Released |publisher=Purdue University Fort Wayne |date=June 18, 2018 |access-date=June 21, 2018}} On March 10, 2019, Konchar recorded 18 points, 10 rebounds, and 10 assists in a 96–70 victory over [[South Dakota Coyotes men's basketball|South Dakota]] in the [[2019 Summit League men's basketball tournament|2019 Summit League tournament]]. It was the first [[double (basketball)|triple-double]] in tournament history.{{cite web|last1=Hoeck|first1=Jeremy|title=Konchar's Triple-Double Propels 'Dons Past USD|url=https://www.yankton.net/sports/article_bff083ba-43b5-11e9-9e67-f78cb7356663.html |website=Yankton Daily Press & Dakotan |access-date=June 5, 2019|date=March 10, 2019}} As a senior for Purdue Fort Wayne, Konchar averaged 19.5 points, 8.6 rebounds, 5.4 assists, and two steals per game, earning first-team All-[[Summit League]] honors for his fourth consecutive season. He compiled 2,065 career points and left as the program's all-time leading scorer.{{cite web|title=John Konchar - 2018-19|url=https://gomastodons.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=7246 |publisher=[[Purdue University Fort Wayne]]|access-date=June 5, 2019}} At the end of the season, [[Tom Henry]], mayor of [[Fort Wayne, Indiana]], proclaimed March 28 as "John Konchar Day."{{cite web|last1=Henry|first1=Tom|last2=Konchar|first2=John|title=John Konchar Day Declared In Fort Wayne|url=https://gomastodons.com/news/2019/3/28/mens-basketball-john-konchar-day-declared-in-fort-wayne.aspx|publisher=[[Purdue University Fort Wayne]]|access-date=June 5, 2019|date=March 28, 2019}} ==Professional career== ===Memphis Grizzlies (2019–2026)=== After going undrafted in the [[2019 NBA draft]], Konchar signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|title=The @memgrizz have signed John Konchar to a two-way contract. Press release below.|url=https://twitter.com/GrizzliesPR/status/1148264315495079937|website=Grizzlies PR on Twitter|access-date=July 8, 2019|date=July 8, 2019}} Konchar made his NBA debut on November 9, 2019, against the [[2019–20 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|url=https://dailymemphian.com/article/8769/as-ja-morant-sits-dallas-mavericks-roll|title=As Ja Morant sits, Dallas Mavericks roll|first=Don|last=Wade|work=Daily Memphian|date=November 9, 2019|access-date=January 2, 2020}} He suffered a calf strain on November 15 and was sidelined for several weeks.{{cite news |title=Grizzlies' John Konchar: Remains sidelined with calf injury |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/grizzlies-john-konchar-remains-sidelined-with-calf-injury/ |access-date=January 17, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=December 4, 2019}} Konchar made 19 appearances for Memphis during his rookie campaign, logging averages of 2.8 points, 2.5 rebounds, and 1.2 assists.{{Cite web|title=John Konchar 2019–20 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3134932/type/nba/year/2020|access-date=February 9, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On November 22, 2020, the Grizzlies announced that they had re-signed Konchar to a multi-year contract.{{cite web|title=Grizzlies re-sign John Konchar to multi-year contract|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-re-sign-john-konchar-to-multi-year-contract-201122|date=November 22, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 22, 2020}} On May 11, 2021, Konchar logged a season-high 18 points on 7-of-10 shooting from the field and 2-of-4 from three along with six rebounds and three assists in 26 minutes of play in a 133–104 win over the [[2020–21 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]].{{Cite web|title=Grizzlies' John Konchar: Best performance of career Tuesday|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/grizzlies-john-konchar-best-performance-of-career-tuesday/|access-date=2021-05-11|website=CBSSports.com}}{{Cite web|title=Postgame Report: Grizzlies pull away from Mavericks, win third straight game|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/postgame/dal-210511|access-date=2021-05-11|website=Memphis Grizzlies}} Konchar made 43 appearances off of the bench for Memphis during the [[2020–21 NBA season]], averaging 4.3 points, 3.0 rebounds, and 1.1 assists.{{Cite web|title=John Konchar 2020–21 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3134932/type/nba/year/2021|access-date=February 9, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} During the Grizzlies' regular season finale on April 10, 2022, Konchar recorded his first career triple-double with 17 points, ten assists, and 13 rebounds in a 110–139 loss to the [[2021–22 Boston Celtics season|Boston Celtics]].{{Cite web |title=Grizzlies' John Konchar: Records first career triple-double |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/grizzlies-john-konchar-records-first-career-triple-double/ |access-date=April 24, 2022 |website=CBS Sports|date=April 11, 2022 }} He made a career-high 72 appearances (including seven starts) for the Grizzlies during the [[2021–22 NBA season]], averaging 4.8 points, 4.6 rebounds, and 1.5 assists.{{Cite web|title=John Konchar 2021–22 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3134932/type/nba/year/2022|access-date=February 9, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On July 7, 2022, Konchar signed a three-year, $19 million contract extension with the Grizzlies.{{Cite web |last=Wojnarowski |first=Adrian |author-link=Adrian |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34206787/guard-john-konchar-agrees-3-year-19-million-extension-memphis-grizzlies |access-date=July 11, 2022 |website=ESPN.com}}{{Cite web |title=Memphis |website=NBA.com}} On November 18, he scored a career-high 19 points, alongside ten rebounds and two assists, in a 121–110 win over the [[2022–23 Oklahoma City Thunder season|Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{Cite web |title=GRIZZLIES BEAT THUNDER, BUT MORANT LEAVES WITH ANKLE INJURY |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200229 |access-date=February 5, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} Konchar made 72 appearances (and a career-high 23 starts) for Memphis during the [[2022–23 NBA season]], recording averages of 5.1 points, 4.3 rebounds, and 1.4 assists.{{Cite web|title=John Konchar 2022–23 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3134932/type/nba/year/2023|access-date=February 9, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} Konchar made 55 appearances (including 23 starts) for Memphis in the [[2023–24 NBA season]], averaging 4.3 points, 4.7 rebounds, and 2.0 assists.{{Cite web|title=John Konchar 2023–24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3134932/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=February 9, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} He played in 46 games (starting four) for the Grizzlies during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], logging averages of 2.4 points, 3.3 rebounds, and 0.9 assists.{{Cite web|title=John Konchar 2024–25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3134932/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=February 9, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On December 15, 2025, it was announced that Konchar would miss at least three weeks after undergoing surgery to repair a torn [[ulnar collateral ligament of thumb|ulnar collateral ligament]] in his left thumb.{{Cite web|title=Grizzlies' John Konchar: To be evaluated in three weeks|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/grizzlies-john-konchar-to-be-evaluated-in-three-weeks/|access-date=December 19, 2025|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} He made 30 total appearances (including one start) for Memphis in the [[2025–26 NBA season]], averaging 3.2 points, 3.1 rebounds, and 1.3 assists.{{Cite web|title=John Konchar 2025–26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3134932/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=February 9, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} === Utah Jazz (2026) === On February 3, 2026, Konchar, [[Jaren Jackson Jr.]], [[Jock Landale]], and [[Vince Williams Jr.]] were traded to the [[Utah Jazz]] in exchange for [[Kyle Anderson (basketball)|Kyle Anderson]], [[Walter Clayton Jr.]], [[Taylor Hendricks]], [[Georges Niang]], and three first-round draft picks.{{Cite web |title=Utah Jazz Acquire Former NBA Defensive Player of the Year and Two-Time NBA All-Star Jaren Jackson Jr. {{!}} Utah Jazz |url=https://utahjazz.com/news/utah-jazz-acquire-former-nba-defensive-player-of-the-year-and-two-time-nba-all-star-jaren-jackson-jr |access-date=2026-02-04 |website=utahjazz.com |language=en}} On April 7, Konchar put up a triple-double with 12 points, 10 rebounds, and 10 assists in a 156–137 loss to the [[2025–26 New Orleans Pelicans season|New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jazzs-john-konchar-rare-triple-double-in-loss/|title=Jazz's John Konchar: Rare triple-double in loss|website=CBS Sports|date=April 7, 2026|access-date=April 11, 2026}} On April 10, Konchar recorded another triple-double with 11 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists off the bench in a 147–101 win over the [[2025–26 Memphis Grizzlies season|Memphis Grizzlies]]. His teammate, [[Bez Mbeng]], also recorded a triple-double with 27 points, 11 rebounds, and 11 assists off the bench, making Mbeng and Konchar the first pair of teammates to each record a triple-double off the bench in a game in NBA history.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/utah-jazz/jazz-news-the-insane-triple-double-history-made-in-tank-off-vs-grizzlies|title=The insane triple-double history made in egregious tank-off Jazz vs. Grizzlies|website=ClutchPoints|last=Ojeda|first=Julian|date=April 11, 2026|access-date=April 11, 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401811036|title=Hinson scores a career-high 30 as the Jazz snap a 10-game skid with win over the Grizzlies|date=April 11, 2026|access-date=April 11, 2026}} On August 29, 2026, Konchar and [[Cody Williams]] were traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in exchange for [[Josh Green (basketball)|Josh Green]], and cash considerations, but was immediately waived.{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Timberwolves Acquire Forwards John Konchar and Cody Williams from Utah Jazz {{!}} Minnesota Timberwolves
